item.title: Align & Flow Yoga — Thu Sep 17, 5:30 PM — Davis Shambhala Meditation Center
item.description:
All classes begin with a meditation and invite mindful movement through attention to breath and physical alignment. In a vinyasa class, we link postures together and move with the breath on the inhale, or the exhale. A typical class involves strength and stability work balanced by flexibility and relaxation. Each class finishes with a reclining rest.
davisyogacollective.com

item.title: Art Farm Exhibition Opening Reception 2026 — Thu Sep 17, 5:30 PM — The Barn Gallery
item.description: Join us for the opening reception of our 19th Annual Art Farm exhibition featuring Art Harvest and Juried Silent Auction artwork. Yolo Arts is pleased to be celebrating our Art Farm exhibition with an opening reception on September 17th, 2026 from 5:30-8:00pm. This exhibition features Northern California artists and artwork inspired by the farmlands of Yolo County. Come and join us as we celebrate the wide variety of artwork entered into the Art Harvest and the Juried Silent Auction! The evening will also feature local wine and refreshments. This event is free and open to the public. The evening reception will include the 6:30 p.m. announcement of the juried prize winners by guest juror Bryan Valenzuela. Three artists will receive cash prizes for Best in Show, Best in Plein Air and Best in Photography. item.title: Self Defense Class — Thu Sep 17, 6:00 PM — Davis Arts Center
item.description:
This is a safe, inclusive opportunity to learn self defense from a dedicated group of martial arts practitioners at the Davis Arts Center. If you have ever felt like you would like to learn a little more about how to defend yourself and your loved ones, and would like to get a little fitness training too, please join us! No experience necessary, start any time. We ask for a $10 donation per class, but you can pay whatever you can.
Source: The Dirt

item.description:

Each session is instructor-led with an easy, approachable art project that anyone can do, designed for connection as much as creativity, no skills needed. Think less “art class” and more “fun night out where you also make something cool.” $30 Adult / $20 Student

item.title: Talk Theology to Me: Questions about Faith & Life — Tue Sep 29, 6:00 PM
item.description:
Iama Embodied Community What questions about faith, God, Scripture, or spirituality have you been carrying around?
**Talk Theology to Me** is an informal, discussion-based gathering for anyone who is curious about faith and the questions that shape our lives. No theological degree—or even a fully formed belief system—is required. Just bring your questions and your willingness to listen and explore. Together, we’ll have a facilitated conversation drawing from **Scripture, theology, and lived experience**. We’ll make room for curiosity, uncertainty, different perspectives, and the kinds of questions that don’t always have easy answers.
### What to expect
* A welcoming, low-pressure conversation * Space to ask honest questions about faith and spirituality * Reflection on Scripture and our own lived experiences * Respect for different perspectives and places in the faith journey * An opportunity to connect with others in a meaningful way

item.description:

Come see 400+ registered student organizations and campus departments who are eager to let the campus community know who they are and what they have to offer. item.title: Davis City Council Meetings — Thu Dec 3, 6:30 PM — City Hall Community Chambers
item.description:
The Davis City Council provides policy direction, establishes goals, and sets priorities for City government. City Council holds regular meetings beginning at 6:30 p.m. on Tuesdays. Most commonly, meetings are held on the first and third Tuesdays of the month, with additional meetings scheduled as needed. The City Council meeting schedule is subject to change.
The Davis City Council meets in the Community Chambers at City Hall, 23 Russell Boulevard. All regular meeting materials are posted at least 72 hours in advance and special meeting materials at least 24 hours in advance.
Visit the City Council site for information on agenda, special meetings, and more.
Source: Hate-Free Together

item.title: Grounded Together: Building Resilience, Connection, and Community — Wed Sep 16, 6:00 PM
item.description:
Iama Embodied Community ***P.S. this is part of a 5 week series, though not required, you are highly encouraged to attend all - No meeting on Oct 7***
Join **Rev. Rola Al-Ashkar** for a five-week journey exploring how our life experiences shape the way we respond to stress, conflict, belonging, and relationships. Through storytelling, guided reflection, and gentle body-centered (somatic) practices, participants will develop tools for greater self-awareness, emotional resilience, and compassionate listening. Whether you're seeking personal growth, healthier relationships, or a deeper sense of connection within our community, this series offers a welcoming and supportive space. No prior experience is necessary. Please register using the following link: [[LINK](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSdxWVImvnFcRLw5on8gH2WFGQfoMnVmNowpxZd9FHajblr2Iw/viewform?usp=send_form)]. **Wednesdays:** Sept. 16, 23, 30; Oct. 14 & 21 6:00 – 8:00 pm
Source: Meetup: Mindful Embodied Spirituality

item.title: Photography Club of Davis — Wed Sep 16, 7:10 PM — Mary L. Stephens Davis Branch Library Blanchard Room
item.description:
The meeting will feature a photo critique of member-submitted images. Critiques tend to be positive learning experiences for both submitters and the general audience. Participants discuss “why does this image work” as well as “why does this image not work” and how the image may be improved. Attendees also learn about the techniques involved. The Photography Club of Davis meets every month on the third Wednesday of the month (except July and August) and welcomes members of the public to attend.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: U.N. "Reboot the Earth" Hackathon — Fri Oct 23 — Peter J. Shields Library at UC Davis
item.description:
In partnership with the United Nations, the UC Davis Open Source Program Office (OSPO) and DataLab will host a "Reboot the Earth" hackathon. Reboot the Earth is a global initiative that addresses local climate and environmental challenges through open source solutions.
Representatives of local agencies championing each challenge track will serve as subject matter experts; students will also have access to mentors.
Who:
The event is hosted by DataLab and the UC Davis Library, and is open to students of all backgrounds and experience levels, from any university or college. No prior hackathon experience is required—just curiosity and an eagerness to build something that matters. Participants are strongly encouraged to form interdisciplinary teams and include peers from a variety of majors. Each team may have a maximum of five people and has to include at least one UC Davis student.
Why:
Contribute to solving a problem in your community
Get experience working on a cross-func

item.title: Davis Farmers Market — Wed Sep 16, 3:00 PM — Central Park
item.description:
Year-round at Central Park in downtown Davis, thousands gather each week to shop for what is grown, raised, and made locally at our markets. We are dedicated to bringing farmers right to your table, so we stay open rain or shine. Walk rows of stalls lined with an array of fruits and vegetables, including certified organic produce, choice meats, chicken, seafood, wine, local eggs and honey. Choose from a variety of fresh-baked goods, plants, flowers and gifts. Enjoy a picnic from one of our many food stands, made from market ingredients. See the vendor list here: https://www.davisfarmersmarket.org/our-sellers/ Farmers Market Hours Central Park: Saturdays 8a–1p (year-round), and Wednesdays 3p–6p (September through March); 4p–8p (April through August) UC Davis – North Quad: Wednesdays 10a–1:30p (fall and spring quarters) Sutter Davis Hospital: Thursdays 10a–1p (May through September) Sutter Medical Center, Sacramento: Thursdays 2:30p–5:30p
Source: The Dirt

item.title: NAMI Yolo County Presents Mental Health in Yolo County Jails Panel — Wed Sep 16, 6:00 PM — Episcopal Church of St. Martin
item.description:
A panel on mental health in Yolo County Jails. Join us for an important community conversation about mental health in Yolo County jails. Designed especially for family members and loved ones, the panel will bring together perspectives from the Yolo County Public Defender’s Office, and the Yolo County Department of Health and Human Services. Panelists will discuss the challenges people with mental health needs may encounter in the jail system, the services and resources available, and how families can better understand and navigate these systems when supporting a loved one. Are you a family member with an incarcerated loved one? Take the family experiences with Yolo County Jail Survey: https://www.surveymonkey.com/r/6XS3CV2.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Author Event: Jason Dove Mark — Wed Sep 16, 6:30 PM — The Avid Reader
item.description: Jason Dove Mark @ The Avid Reader Wednesday Sep 16th, 2026 | 6:30 PM – 7:30 PM About the Book – The Earth Said Remember Me As the climate emergency worsens and biodiversity shrinks, we somehow get used to it. We struggle to remember what summers were like before the unrelenting heat, in those years before wildfires became an annual routine. We adapt, we normalize. Scientists call this “shifting baseline syndrome,” and they warn that it’s why we are increasingly sleepwalking toward disaster. In this inspiring manifesto, environmental advocate and longtime editor-in-chief of Sierra magazine Jason Dove Mark offers antidotes that everyone can use to resist ecological amnesia and make lasting progress to repair and revive a livable planet. He puts forth four simple but powerful rules for a life lived in communion with the Earth: Go outside Bear witness Make a record Pass it on From the mountains of California to the lakes of Wisconsin and across the lush forests of his beloved Pacif
